faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does Overflowing Court disable other Overflowing Courts? Other cards with "Court" in the title?
faq.a: Yes. Any card with the exact word "Court" in the title will be disabled. For example, Mock Court and Court Jester would be disabled, but Courtesan Thaïs is not.

faq.q: For Mock Court, how does this extra cost work?
faq.a:
For each ordinary minion that you would summon, you must pay 1 mana at the moment it would be summoned into the realm (for each copy of Mock Court). This is not an additional casting cost; it's a summoning cost. If you can pay it, you must. If you are summoning multiple ordinary minions simultaneously (e.g. Border Militia) and can't afford to pay for all of them, you may choose which ones you pay for. Any that you cannot pay for are not summoned.
This effect applies to ordinary token minions (e.g. Skeletons, Frogs, Foot Soldiers) that are summoned without being cast, as well as ordinary minions that you cast normally (e.g. Apprentice Wizard).

faq.q: Can you give a complicated Kairos example?
faq.a:
Enjoy this one:
I have an Kettletop Leprechaun on Gnome Hollows in square 8.
You have a Cloud Spirit on Cloud City in square 3.
The realm gets archived. Then:
Cloud City moves to square 9 and you summon Bluecap Knockers there.
I cast a Grim Guisarme into the hands of my Leprechaun, who moves to square 9.
I cast a House Arn Bannerman into the Gnome Hollows.
Then, Kairos dies. All of the following happen simultaneously:
My Kettletop Leprechaun returns to square 8; even though it's a Gnome Hollows and the Leprechaun has 3 power due to the House Arn Bannerman, remember that the "return" effect is not movement and is not considered "entering."
The Grim Guisarme is not an archived card, and it remains where it is on square 9. Carried artifacts move whenever their bearer moves, but returning is not a movement effect, so the artifact doesn't automatically come with the Leprechaun.
The Cloud Spirit and Cloud City return to square 3; this is not movement, and thus Bluecap Knockers does not prevent it. The Bluecap Knockers find themselves in the void and are banished. There is a Grim Guisarme in the void on square 9 now. Had there been a site on square 3, it would have been banished as Cloud City returned to that square.
When in doubt, always apply the Golden Rule, but especially with Kairos!

faq.q: In limited play (i.e. Sealed and Draft), may I cast Serava Townsfolk and Eltham Townsfolk from outside my card pool?
faq.a: Yes! Those cards have "Townsfolk" in their name, and are thus covered by the "specifically named card" rule for limited games. You do not need them in your collection in draft or sealed. You still need to meet the threshold requirement to cast them, though!

faq.q: How is the facing for the Trap determined?
faq.a: When you conjure the Sentinel Trap into the realm, choose a cardinal direction to be its initial facing. It then rotates from there. If it is teleported, the controller of the teleport effect can choose which cardinal direction it ends up facing.

faq.q: How do I calculate the difference in cost of the two minions?
faq.a: Start with the cost of the Evil minion in your hand, then subtract the cost of the Mortal at the Pond. Remember that costs cannot be negative, so if the result is below zero, treat it as zero instead.

faq.q: Can I summon Evil Twin to a non-surface location if it will be copying a minion that has the appropriate ability (e.g. summon to an underground location while copying a Root Spider)?
faq.a: No. The Evil Twin only gains the abilities as enters the realm, and you must declare its summoning location at the time you cast it, before it enters.

faq.q: If I Detonate a minion with the Lethal ability, is the damage from Detonate Lethal?
faq.a: No, the source of the damage is the Detonate spell itself, not the exploding minion.

faq.q: What does it mean to "fly to" something? Does it have to be the shortest possible path or any valid path?
faq.a: Refer to the article on ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) to see how an ability like this works.

faq.q: Can this Pick Up and carry enemy minions?
faq.a: Yes, the coach will carry anyone!

faq.q: What happens if there's a silence or disable effect somewhere in the realm that affects minions (e.g. Root Spider, Silence aura)?
faq.a: Yog-Sothoth will be disabled or silenced by the effect, but will continue to occupy all locations since its size is a characteristic. This usually means Yog-Sothoth will be banished, since it can no longer safely occupy void locations!

faq.q: Who controls the Consecrated Ground that the site transforms into?
faq.a: Since the site transforms, the controller of the site will not change. Whoever controlled the site that was warded will control the Consecrated Ground. If that site had no controller, no one will control the Consecrated Ground.

faq.q: What happens if the Bogeyman is Silenced or Disabled while carrying enemies?
faq.a: As per the rules about Carrying Units, if the Bogeyman loses his ability to carry enemies, they will be dropped and no longer carried or disabled themselves.

faq.q: Does tapping to free a trapped minion count as interacting with the realm?
faq.a: Yes, tapping to free a minion from its cocoon is activating a special ability, and counts as interacting with the realm.

faq.q: What is a "new site"?
faq.a: A site where this card has not stopped since entering the realm.

faq.q: Can this choose to drop the minion it is carrying?
faq.a: Yes, abilities which allow a unit to pick up other units also allow them to drop them.

faq.q: What happens to the site that is replaced?
faq.a: The site being replaced is banished.

faq.q: If this stops carrying a minion can it pick up another minion?
faq.a: Yes, it can pick up another minion, or the same minion again.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a: Allies which are nearby to the Marrows, including themselves, can't be forcibly submerged, e.g. ((Atlantean Fate)), ((Drown)), ((Call of the Sea)), etc. Nearby allies can still choose to submerge when taking their own steps via their own submerge ability.

faq.q: What does "drowns" mean?
faq.a: A minion "drowns" if it dies due to being underwater without also having the submerge ability. You control the resulting Skeleton.

faq.q: How long does this effect last?
faq.a: When Bane of Aventis' Genesis ability resolves, its controller will gain control of all Warded minions nearby. This change of control is indefinite, and will last even after those minions ))lose(( their Wards.

faq.q: Who decides where the minion steps?
faq.a: The controller of Screamer.

faq.q: Since this "counts as Grey Wolves" does that mean I can include any number of it in my spellbook?
faq.a: No. The phrase "counts as Grey Wolves" means that other cards will see it as being named "Grey Wolves" in addition to its normal name. You still must follow rarity restrictions.

faq.q: Does this actually target the Avatar?
faq.a: Yes. If your opponent casts this and targets your Warded avatar, you will not draw any cards and the Ward will break. Normal targeting rules apply (e.g. a spellcaster in the void or subsurface couldn't target an avatar with this magic, since they aren't in the same region).

faq.q: Does the Spellcaster have to be a unit to tap and release the Demon?
faq.a: Yes.  Only units can tap, so a spellcaster artifact or site would be unable to release the demon.

faq.q: When my opponent casts a minion spell with Voidwalk, can they choose The Void as its summoning location, even though it's my site?
faq.a: Yes! It is a void, so they can choose to cast their Voidwalk minions to here if they wish.

faq.q: Can I cast this onto my opponent's site in an outer column?
faq.a: No, this is an additional casting restriction; it does not allow you to summon Forsaken to locations you normally could not.

faq.q: What is the timing for the resolution of this spell?
faq.a:
Choose an ally, declare its movement steps, placing them on the Storyline, then resolve those steps. Repeat for each ally.
That is, you declare and resolve each ally’s steps before proceeding to the next ally. If you gain more allies during the resolution, you may move them too; keep repeating the effect until each ally has moved.

faq.q: Are minions along the path affected even if they have stealth?
faq.a: Yes! Projectiles do not hit stealth minions, but Snowball is just using the projectile to draw a path. It doesn't matter what units are hit, all of them along the path are rolled up in the snowball and pulled along!

faq.q: Does this affect spells drawn by things like Morgana le Fay and the Omphaloi?
faq.a:
Yes.  Though those cards end up in another zone, they count as being drawn by the player, and will count against the one spell that can be drawn per turn.  
For example, if a player draws a site at the start of their turn and then plays [[Morgana le Fay]], Morgana will only draw 1 spell into her hand, resulting in a total of only 1 spell drawn by that player that turn.  See the Only It Can Cast entry for more information.

faq.q: How does this Magic work?
faq.a:
Onslaught creates an ongoing effect which lasts the duration of your turn and continually prevents your units from being immobilized, silenced, or disabled. A minion cast after Onslaught resolves would be protected, and would gain +1 power and Charge.
Note that Onslaught does not remove any ongoing effects which may be disabling, silencing or immobilizing your units, it just suppresses them for the duration of your turn. 
For example, if you play Onslaught and then summon a [[Slumbering Giantess]], her Genesis ability will still resolve, and she will be disabled when the effect of Onslaught wears off. For the duration of your turn, however, she will have +1 power and Charge, and will ignore the disable effect from her Genesis ability.

faq.q: Does the ally die if it didn't take enough damage from the fights to kill it?
faq.a: No. If the fights with those enemies wouldn't normally kill your ally, your ally will live!

faq.q: Does the Hyena stop being a Beast if it becomes a Demon?
faq.a: No, it will be both a Demon and a Beast.

faq.q: Does conjuring this into the realm count as "stopping"?
faq.a: No, something must move in order to stop, and conjuring something into the realm is not movement. To trigger, the Flame has to move from one location to another.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a: Whenever ))Realm-Eater(( attacks a site and strikes it, that site is destroyed and the ))Realm-Eater(( gains an ongoing effect causing it to be immobile. You can activate ))Realm-Eater's(( digest ability to remove one instance of this immobilizing effect, but if you have attacked and destroyed multiple sites you must digest each one.

faq.q: Does this play ability allow me to break normal site placement rules?
faq.a: Yes! You may play this site to replace an Elite or Unique site, even if that site isn't adjacent to your existing sites.

faq.q: Does this destroy artifacts underneath the site, or just ones on the surface?
faq.a: Artifacts both above and below the site are destroyed.

faq.q: Do I have to reveal the traded artifacts?
faq.a: Yes, you must reveal them to ensure it is a fair trade.

faq.q: What happens if Realm-Eater cannot be immobilized due to some effect (e.g. Tabula Rasa, Onslaught)?
faq.a: For as long as the effect is being applied, ))Realm((-Eater can ignore the ongoing effect caused by eating sites. If that effect is removed, ))Realm((-Eater will no longer be immune to the lethargy caused by eating so much, and will be immobilized if they have not cleared the ongoing effects by digesting the sites.

faq.q: Can I attempt to fill the Hemogoblet if it's already full?
faq.a: No, you must empty it first.

faq.q: What happens if Lilith summons a minion with an end of turn ability (e.g. Infernal Legion)?
faq.a: Their ability will not trigger this turn.

faq.q: Where does the stolen spell go?
faq.a: It goes to a separate zone as if the Pith Imp was carrying the spell; it does not go to your hand. You may look at the spell and your opponent may not (though they do get to see the spell at the moment you steal it).

faq.q: Will this affect minions in the void or underground?
faq.a: No. Because you are looking for adjacent minions, not an adjacent site, you cannot ignore regional boundaries.

faq.q: If I cast a Magic with X in the cost, does the copy have the same value of X too?
faq.a: Yes. The Orb copies the spell after costs have been paid, so X is a set value.

faq.q: If the damage from this trigger is prevented or redirected, do I still gain 1 life?
faq.a: No, you must deal at least 1 point of damage with the ability to gain any life.

faq.q: What if the Mortal's location is one where Jack would be silenced? Or disabled?
faq.a:
When Jack the Ripper is cast (before he even enters the realm!), his ability is put on the storyline to resolve in the future, when he enters the realm.
Silenced upon entering the realm: His ability is already on the storyline, so it still resolves. (A silenced minion can still kill other minions.) He does lose stealth due to silence.
Disabled upon entering the realm: His ability is already on the storyline, but when it goes to resolve, he cannot actually kill anyone, since being disabled prevents a minion from taking any actions granted by an effect. He will also lose stealth due to being disabled.

faq.q: What happens to Morgana's hand if she is transformed into something else? A frog, for instance?!
faq.a: If Morgana is transformed, the ongoing effect which created her hand of cards will continue to apply, and the hand will continue to exist. If Morgana's new form does not have the ability to cast spells, she will not be able to cast them, but if she becomes a spellcaster again she will still have access to her hand.

faq.q: Can I banish an evil ally from my cemetery or hand?
faq.a: No, you can only choose an ally in the realm to be banished by Rasputin's ability.

faq.q: How does this interact with effects like Browse or Kelp Caverns, which do not say to search, but have you look at cards instead?
faq.a: If the effect does not use the word "search" in its text, it will not be limited by Haystack.

faq.q: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?
faq.a: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

faq.q: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?
faq.a: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

faq.q: Does this end of turn ability cause the Beast to lose stealth?
faq.a: No, as it is a triggered ability it does not cause the Beast to interact with the realm.

faq.q: How does this ability interact with Flooded sites?
faq.a: The Flooded ability gives a site a minimum of 1 water threshold, making it a water site. Even a bearer of Key to the City will see the water threshold and treat it as a water site. e.g. It will die in the subsurface if it doesn't have Submerge, it can't be forcefully Burrowed, etc.

faq.q: Can a unit be moved through the top border of this site by force?
faq.a:
No, assuming the unit does not have the Airborne ability.  Effects which drag/push/pull a unit cannot cause it to move through the top border of this site while on the ground.  For instance, a non-Airborne minion cannot use  [[Grapple Shot]] to pass through this border, and a [[Pudge Butcher]] cannot pull a non-Airborne unit through it.
Teleport effects do not pass through borders, however, and are not considered movement on the ground, so they can allow a unit to ))move(( to a location on the other side.

faq.q: Can I modify the cost of (5)?
faq.a: Yes! If you have Philosopher's Stone and you're playing as Harbinger, you could perhaps cast minions for a mere (3)!

faq.q: Do I draw a spell if my opponent's minion enters the realm tapped?
faq.a: No. This ability only triggers when a minion goes from being untapped to tapped while nearby the Idol.

faq.q: Can this ability be activated multiple times per turn?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you pay 1 mana for each time you wish to activate it.

faq.q: When this is destroyed because it was damaged, who is responsible for the destruction?
faq.a: The source of the damage is responsible, thanks to the golden rule!  This will trigger effects like [[Vindictive Nation]], and will be prevented by effects like [[Order of the Sacred Oak]].

faq.q: Does the minion that's being summoned from elsewhere enter the realm for a moment before it's banished?
faq.a: No, it doesn't ever enter the realm. For example, it will not trigger a Genesis, it will not get a Lance, it will not trigger a Mariner's Curse, etc. It doesn't actually enter the realm at all, since this is a replacement effect.

faq.q: What happens if Damion and his Ghouls are all damaged simultaneously by a Poison Nova?
faq.a: Damion dies from the Lethal damage but is still in the realm at the time his Ghouls would be marked for death, so his ability protects them. Each Ghoul will have one damage for the rest of the turn. (Lethal is relevant only while the damage is applied, and is not an ongoing quality of the damage after it is applied.)

faq.q: Can this target sub-surface minions?
faq.a: Yes.  The minion must be nearby to the site, which means it must be near one of the site's locations.  This means that minions which are underground (or underwater, if the Shrike Orchard is flooded) can be targeted by this effect.

faq.q: If I cast a Magic as a Spirit minion, will Orb of Ba'al Berith copy it?
faq.a: Good try, but no. You're casting it as a minion, so the game sees it as a Minion spell, not a Magic spell.

faq.q: When is the power of the minion checked to see if it's small enough to summon to any site?
faq.a: You check at the time of casting, before the minion enters the realm. This means that you can summon a Vengeful Heir to any site, even if it enters the realm as a minion which would be too large to work with Spore Sprouts normally, for example.

faq.q: If a unit moves into the site on the same turn, but after Geyser has been cast, does it gain Airborne?
faq.a: No, the minion must be at the site when Geyser resolves to gain Airborne.

faq.q: Can I push an oversized unit?
faq.a: Yes, choose a cardinal direction and push the oversized unit one step in that direction as long as no part of the unit would change regions.

faq.q: There's a promotional version of this card with the name "Grandmeowster Wizard." Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have two copies of each in my deck?
faq.a: No, treat "Grandmeowster Wizard" as being named "Grandmaster Wizard" for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

faq.q: Is this forced movement?
faq.a: No, the enemy is taking their own step which can benefit from movement abilities such as Voidwalk or Airborne.

faq.q: If the minion is not dragged to Gargantula's location, does it still get disabled? What if the minion is already at Gargantula's location?
faq.a: Gargantula must be at the same location as the minion to wrap it in her web, so if the minion cannot be dragged there it will not be disabled. However, if it already shares a location with Gargantula, she will cocoon it.

faq.q: Does this cause a zero power unit to deal 2 damage when striking?
faq.a: Yes, this effect will cause zero power units to strike for 2 damage.

faq.q: What does "Avatars here can't leave" mean?
faq.a:
Avatars currently under the Sphere of Animosity can't enter locations not occupied by the Sphere. This means they can't move to those locations, or be moved by force.
Note that when a site moves, it carries along cards of normal size with it, and those cards do not count as entering a new location. This means that a moving site can carry an Avatar out of the Sphere.

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect if I sacrifice a card that has multiple types (e.g. Automaton) ?
faq.a: When you sacrifice a card that has multiple types, you may specify which type your opponent must match. For example, if you sacrifice one automaton (Minion and Artifact), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an artifact, your choice (not both). Similarly, if you're playing as Enchantress and you sacrifice an animated aura (Minion and Aura), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an aura, your choice (not both).

faq.q: What does "can't attack you" actually mean?
faq.a: The other player can't attack anything you control (units or sites).

faq.q: Once this is in play, do I put cards into the cemetery that I own or the cemetery that I control?
faq.a: You always put your cards into the cemetery you own (the one nearby your deck).

faq.q: What is a “connected river”?
faq.a:
Connected rivers are a contiguous group of adjacent sites with River in their name, regardless of who controls them, and which contains River Rapids.
River Rapids is, by definition, connected to itself, even if it is not connected to any other Rivers.

faq.q: Can I reveal fewer than three minions?
faq.a: Yes! You can reveal up to three different Evil minions from the searched spells and draw them.

faq.q: What happens if my opponent searches my spellbook but doesn't see this card when searching?
faq.a:
If it's in your spellbook and they could see it, The Inquisition will trigger and be summoned! Tell your opponent that the card is in your spellbook and reveal it to them.
If your opponent is only searching a limited part of your spellbook (e.g. Haystack), The Inquisition will only trigger if it was in the part of your spellbook that was actually searched. If there's a question, a judge can verify that The Inquisition wasn't there.

faq.q: There's a promotional version of this card with the name "Apurrentice Wizard." Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have four copies of each in my deck?
faq.a: No, treat "Apurrentice Wizard" as being named "Apprentice Wizard" for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a:
Any time your Avatar would take damage, you reduce that damage by 2, to a minimum of 0. Note that an enemy striking one of your sites causes life loss to your Avatar, not damage; life loss is not affected by this ability.
Each source of damage is reduced by 2. For example, if you attack and three Foot Soldiers defend together, you take 0 damage since each Foot Soldier would do 1 damage, which you reduce. As another example, if you are hit by an Arcane Barrage for 5, you take 0 damage, since each projectile would do 1 damage, which you reduce.

faq.q: When casting a spell from my cemetery that would banish itself after casting (e.g. Ghostfire), can I choose not to pay the extra cost to keep it from banishing itself?
faq.a: No. You must pay the (2) before even casting the spell, as a separate cost. Once you actually cast it, you resolve the effect normally and your access tax has already been paid.

faq.q: Can I choose to banish only some minions from the targeted location?
faq.a: No, if you choose to use this ability you must banish all minions at the targeted location with 2 or less power.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a:
The Abomination takes damage as if it is one unit, but the player causing the damage can choose which part or parts of the Abomination it applies to (after damage reduction, if any). Once a part has enough damage assigned to kill it, it's removed. When the last part of the Abomination is destroyed, so is the Abomination.
For example, I have an Abomination with 5 + 4 + 3 power, and you are dealing it 7 damage from a Major Explosion. You can assign 3 and 4 damage, destroying those parts, and it's left with 5 power. Alternately, if it were my own Major Explosion, I could assign 3 damage to the 5-power part, and 3 damage to the 4-power part, and 1 damage to 3-power part. It's left with 5+4+3 power, with some damage on each of those parts (which will be removed normally at end of turn).

If an effect would destroy or kill the Abomination outright, including taking Lethal damage, all of its parts are killed. If an effect would banish the Abomination, all of it is banished.

faq.q: When does this ability trigger?
faq.a: If an effect requires you to reveal it from your hand, or from your spellbook, or if your opponent searches your spellbook.

faq.q: Does Spire satisfy the Spire Lich?
faq.a: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

faq.q: How does this interact with damage prevention effects?
faq.a: Damage prevention effects on the avatar will still apply to the damage from Searing Truth.

faq.q: What counts as a "fire spell"?
faq.a: Once a minion, aura, or artifact enters the realm, it is no longer considered a "spell." Magic never enters the realm, so it is still considered a spell while it is resolving. In effect, Lava Salamander is immune to fire Magic.

faq.q: If some effect prevents me from giving the Peace Offering to the other player (i.e. King Arthur), can they attack me on their next turn?
faq.a: Yes. If the other player does not end up controlling the Peace Offering after the ability resolves and passives are applied, you have not successfully given it to them, and they will be free to attack you.

faq.q: What does it mean to "permanently lose stealth"?
faq.a: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

faq.a: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

faq.a: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

faq.q: My minion starts nearby the Mask and thus must attack. During my Move and Attack mandatory action, my minion moves so that it's no longer near the Mask. Do I still have to attack?
faq.a: No, since you do not actually attack until after moving. If your minion is no longer nearby the Mask, you are not required to attack after moving.

faq.q: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?
faq.a: The non-active player chooses a minion, then the active player chooses a minion. Then all other minions are killed. The non-active player resolves any triggered abilities (like deathrite), and finally the active player resolves their triggered abilities.

faq.q: Can Jack be cast to a Mortal in a region other than the surface?
faq.a: Yes, but if cast to the void, he will be banished before the rest of his cast ability can resolve. If summoned underground or underwater (or to any location with an effect that would kill him) he will die before he can complete his task as well, assuming he doesn't immediately gain the ability to survive in that location.  This means he will neither Silence nor Kill his prey.

faq.q: If Peace Offering leaves the realm, does the truce still apply?
faq.a: Yes, once the Peace Offering has been given to your opponent, they can't attack you next turn, regardless of what happens to the Peace Offering after that.

faq.q: Can my allied minion tempt an enemy in a different region to take a step closer?
faq.a: Yes, as long as they occupy a nearby site, they can be above or below that site.  However, they cannot be tempted to take a step into a region they couldn't normally move into (e.g. they cannot be made to step underground if they do not have Burrowing).

faq.q: What happens if the minion which leaves this site can't be warded (e.g. it has a Ward already or it's Evil)?
faq.a: The Ward remains on the site, as it cannot be transferred.

faq.q: What if there are multiple Kairos's in play?
faq.a: Whenever a new Kairos archives the realm, that becomes the most recent snapshot for all Kairos deathrite effects. That is, there is only a single archive of the realm at a time. Archivists unite!

faq.q: Stretch my avatar? You're pulling my leg! Does this make my avatar an oversized unit now?
faq.a: Pulling both arms and both legs actually but, yes! Your avatar will now be an oversized unit!

faq.q: How is this resolved if either the artifact or the bearer cannot be pulled?
faq.a: If the bearer of the artifact cannot be pulled, but the artifact can, the Red Rock pulls the artifact out of the bearer's hands. If the artifact cannot be pulled, neither the bearer nor the artifact are pulled.

faq.q: What do X cost spells count as for this effect?
faq.a: Unless resolving on the storyline, X cost spells are treated as costing zero.

faq.q: How does forced movement affect minions in the Cage?
faq.a: Due to the golden rule, only teleportation-based forced movement effects can move minions out of the Cage; non-teleportation, forced movement effects can't move the locked minions away from the Cage. For example, [[Blink]] or [[Swap]] would allow a minion to escape, but [[River Rapids]], [[Riptide]], or [[Scatter]] would not.

faq.q: Does this strike a unit at the location it was summoned to?
faq.a: No, since it will enter that location before its Genesis ability begins to resolve. It will only strike a unit at each of the two new locations it enters while resolving its Genesis.

faq.q: What happens if my opponent plays a site nearby Cursed Land that would silence it (e.g. Fields of Phyxis, Smokestacks of Gnaak)?
faq.a: They will not lose life. This is because Cursed Land's ability is a triggered ability, but [[Fields of Phyxis]] and [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] both have passive abilities which apply ongoing effects, and ongoing effects are applied before triggers.

faq.q: If the 3 damage is reduced, redirected away from "here", or prevented, do I still heal 3?
faq.a: No, the full 3 damage must be dealt to the targeted minion here in order to heal 3.

faq.q: If the allied minion was already tapped before using this ability on them, do they still gain Ward?
faq.a: Yes, you resolve as much of this ability as you can. Granting the Ward is not contingent on the minion being untapped beforehand.

faq.q: What happens if the Bogeyman's power is reduced while carrying enemies?
faq.a: Only check that the enemy is weaker at the time that the Bogeyman targets them with the Pick Up ability. If the Bogeyman loses power or the enemy gains power later, the enemy can still continue to be carried.

faq.q: What if there are fewer than three cards in the chosen collection?
faq.a: You banish all of the remaining cards.

faq.q: How does this interact with effects which modify healing (e.g. River of Blood)?
faq.a: You banish all dead minions, count them, and then heal once for a total amount equal to the number of dead minions which were banished. [[River of Blood]] would halve, rounding down, that final total.

faq.q: If Draconian Bonekite, Sir Pelleas, and Azuridge Caravan are all in the realm, can I choose to keep the Caravan and another minion?
faq.a: No, you cannot save Azuridge Caravan and other minions. Since Azuridge Caravan counts as all minion types, you cannot save it and any other minion with a type since they will always have a shared type.

faq.q: Are the minions and artifacts targeted by the allies which drag them down, or by the caster of Grasping Ground?
faq.a: The caster of Grasping Ground must be able to target the minions and artifacts which will be be dragged down by their allies.

faq.q: What happens if this is cast from a cemetery by Deathspeaker?
faq.a: You can still use its optional alternate summoning ability to transform an artifact into the Mimic, and then the Mimic will be banished.

faq.q: How do I properly resolve this effect?
faq.a:
Lord of Greed may and must take a carriable artifact from anywhere in the realm, including from another unit sharing a location with him. In this case, "elsewhere" means anywhere other than Lord of Greed's hands! He will take from allies as well.
This does not target the artifact, so even artifacts carried by minions with stealth are not safe from Lord of Greed.

faq.q: If there are minions with multiple types in the realm, can I choose what type they count as when resolving The Flood? (e.g. I control Draconian Bonekite and Wyvern.
faq.a: They are both of their minion types at all times. Though each minion has another minion type in addition to Dragon in their type line, you can only choose one! You can only save one Dragon from the flood!

faq.q: Can I cast this on my Avatar when my opponent and I are both on Death's Door to win the game?
faq.a: Yes. Thanks to the golden rule, your avatar will not die until after finishing all of its fights.

faq.q: Can this Genesis effect drag a minion into a different region?
faq.a: Yes, due to the golden rule. Because avatars cannot enter non-surface locations, if one is being dragged by this effect they will be dragged as far as they can while staying within the surface region.

faq.q: Can Aino step across the top and bottom edges of the realm if she already has Stealth?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does this prevent minions from being cast from other "hand" zones (e.g. Morgana le Fay, or an Omphalos)?
faq.a: Yes. The Order prevents minions from being summoned from anywhere except directly from a player's hand.

faq.q: Does the chosen minion need to have the Spellcaster ability to cast the spell which they draw from this Genesis ability?
faq.a: No, they gain the Spellcaster ability specifically for the purpose of casting that spell. See the rules for "Only They Can Cast" for specific details.

faq.q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
faq.a: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

faq.q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
faq.a: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

faq.q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
faq.a: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

faq.q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
faq.a: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a:
When you summon Mimic, you can choose to summon it normally, or instead you can choose a carriable artifact anywhere in the realm. That artifact is banished, and the Mimic is placed at the artifact's location instead as it transforms. 
You control the Mimic, and if the artifact did not enter the realm this turn, the Mimic doesn't have Summoning Sickness. It turns out that artifact was a Mimic in disguise all along!

faq.q: Does "no minion is Evil" mean they are no longer considered a Demon, Monster or Undead?
faq.a: Minions will still keep their Demon, Monster and Undead types! They simply are no longer Evil, and will not be affected by things which specifically affect Evil.

faq.q: What if the Magic is cast by something other than a unit?
faq.a: The Sturmgeist only hears spells cast by enemies, which are units. Spells cast by artifacts (e.g. Omphalos) or sites (e.g. River of Flame) will not trigger its ability.

faq.q: Do I summon a copy the turn I first summon the Locusts?
faq.a: Yes! At the end of the turn you first summon them, they will see that there are no "new" Locusts (meaning Locusts summoned by the triggered ability), and thus summon a copy. The following turn if you still have two in the realm, you'll only get one more.

faq.q: What does "When the star falls" mean?
faq.a: At the end of each of your turns, during step 1 of the end phase, add a counter to Falling Star. When you add the third counter, you immediately summon a minion and resolve the rest of this effect, then dispel Falling Star.

faq.q: Must one of my units carry this to gain the mana?
faq.a: Yes! If no one is carrying it, it isn't controlled by you. Without a controller, the Ether Core provides mana to no one. Remember that carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled!

faq.q: If I activate this ability and then move a minion nearby the Horror, does the minion become disabled?
faq.a: No. This ability disables minions that are nearby the Horror when the ability is activated. A minion moving nearby after that moment will not be disabled.

faq.q: Who chooses what minions of each type are saved from The Flood?
faq.a: The controller of the spell.

faq.q: Does this ability damage units at locations in other regions?
faq.a: Yes, one unit at each location in every square in the cardinal direction chosen! This will include surface and subsurface of sites, as well as the void. Beware the ))evil(( eye!

faq.q: Who controls the Desecrated Ground that the site transforms into?
faq.a: Since the site transforms, the controller of the site will not change. Whoever controlled the site that was struck will control the Desecrated Ground. If that site had no controller, no one will control the Desecrated Ground.

faq.q: What happens if the minion stops being Evil while under this effect (e.g. due to Persecutor's Brand wearing off, or Saint of Redemption entering play)?
faq.a: The target only needs to be Evil when the spell is cast and resolves. It will continue to be be disabled, even if it stops being Evil later, until an adjacent Spellcaster taps specifically to release it.

faq.q: If I cast a spell with an additional cost (e.g. Craterize), do I need to pay the additional cost again?
faq.a: No. The Orb copies the spell after costs have been paid.

faq.q: If the tempted enemy has multiple equally closer steps, who chooses the specific step taken?
faq.a: The caster of this spell determines among the equally closer choices.

faq.q: What is the proper way to resolve the timing for this spell?
faq.a:
Choose an ally, then declare an enemy near it to fight, putting that fight on the storyline. Resolve the fight, including any deathrite abilities of the enemy, and place it in the cemetery if it died. Then, repeat the process one fight at a time until the chosen ally has fought all nearby enemies. Finally, if your ally took enough damage, it will now die.
That is, you declare and resolve each fight before proceeding to the next one.
For example, you play Blaze of Glory on your Autumn Unicorn. I have an Estranged Loner, Muddy Pigs, and my Avatar nearby. You choose to fight my avatar first, so I lose 4 life. Then you choose to fight the Estranged Loner. It dies, I summon a Horrible Hybrids, and the Estranged Loner goes to my cemetery. Then you fight the Horrible Hybrids, it dies too, and goes to my cemetery. Then you fight the Muddy Pigs, they die, I gain 3 life, then they go to my cemetery. Finally, your Unicorn has taken enough damage to die, so it would trigger any deathrite abilities now (if it had any), and then go to your cemetery. A Blaze of Glory indeed!

faq.q: I strike your minion, which is nearby the Drums. Then, you redirect the damage to a bodyguard (e.g. Royal Bodyguard, Sir Gawain), who is not nearby the Drums. Does your bodyguard take lethal damage?
faq.a: No. If the minion actually being damaged is not near the Drums, the damage is not Lethal.

faq.q: Can I choose to save a minion that has no minion type e.g. Maiden, Mother, Crone?
faq.a: No, since Maiden, Mother, Crone has no type it cannot be saved from being submerged.

faq.q: If I summon a minion to a location affected by Hillock Basilisk, will my minion's Genesis ability resolve?
faq.a: Yes, the minion will not be at rest until all of its events on the storyline are resolved, including its Genesis ability.

faq.q: Can Imposter wear masks of Avatars with pre-game or setup abilities, and if so, what happens?
faq.a:
Yes, you can wear masks of those avatars, and you simply ignore their pre-game or setup abilities since the game has already started by the time you put on the mask. For example:
You can use [[Pathfinder]]'s ability even though your atlas has duplicate sites.
You don't get to pick a Unique Dragon as [[Dragonlord]]. (Probably not a good choice of masks.)
You don't roll for summoning portals as [[Harbinger]]. (Probably not a good choice of masks.)
Your decks and card sleeves remain as-is for [[Magician]].  (Probably not a good choice of masks.)

faq.q: If I transform an enemy minion into a Monster from my hand or Horrible Hybrids from my collection, who controls it?
faq.a: The controller of the minion does not change when transforming, so in that case your opponent would control it. Note cards always go to their owner's cemetery so when that minion dies it will go to your cemetery.

faq.q: Can I transform a Mortal I do not control into Evil from my hand?
faq.a: Yes, though since it is a transform effect, control of the transformed minion will not change. The player who controlled the Mortal will control the Evil that came from your hand.

faq.q: When hemogoblet is emptied, do I gain mana or life equal to the power of the minion at that moment, or the power of the minion at the time of sacrifice?
faq.a: At the time of sacrifice. Make note of the minion's power when you fill the hemogoblet!

faq.q: Can I play this with only one Hellhound in my collection?
faq.a: Yes. You will only summon that one [[Hellhound]].

faq.q: Can you tap minions with summoning sickness for this effect?
faq.a: Yes, it's part of the effect of the spell, not strictly a cost being paid, so you can tap your allies that have summoning sickness for this effect.  Note that only untapped units can be tapped, however.

faq.q: If these die during my end phase, does their deathrite cause the game to proceed to the next end phase, essentially skipping my opponent's turn?
faq.a: No, when the deathrite resolves during the end phase it does not cause the game to proceed to the next end phase, as you're already in the end phase.

faq.q: Does this effect kill minions near the Albatross, or near the killer?
faq.a: The minions near the killer die.

faq.q: If Persecutor brands a minion, are they still considered evil by that player's cards while the Saint of Redemption is in play?
faq.a: No, the Saint redeems all minions, and even the Persecutor's brand will not condemn a redeemed soul!

faq.q: Who controls the summoned minion?
faq.a: The controller of Lilith. Note cards always go to the cemetery of their owner, regardless of their controller.

faq.q: What is the updated text for the front of the Druid?
faq.a:
Tap -> Play or draw a site. If this is your first turn, summon Tawny here.
Tap -> Summon Bruin here. Flip this card.

faq.q: How does this effect work?
faq.a: Cards with the printed Mortal type become Beasts, lose the Mortal type, and are silenced.

faq.q: Can Magic spells which cause an ally to target a unit (e.g. Shatter Strike) select the bearer of Amulet as the target?
faq.a: Yes, because the ally is doing the targeting, not the Magic spell.

faq.q: Does this strike my avatar even if I summon it somewhere else?
faq.a: Yes, Dreadwing will strike your avatar even if they don't share a location when its Genesis resolves.

faq.q: If I happen to play a Lone Tower from the top of my atlas, will the mana from the Genesis ability also be doubled? What about mana from Abundance?
faq.a: Yes. Any mana that the site produces, including via any abilities, will be doubled.

faq.q: Can my opponent use this effect as well?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: If I choose a minion that has no Deathrite ability, does it still gain stealth?
faq.a: Yes, it will still gain stealth.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a: If the Regurgitator has an empty belly and there are any dead minions, you must fill its belly by banishing one. If it has a full belly, you must empty it by shooting a projectile. If it has an empty belly and there are no dead minions, nothing happens.

faq.q: What happens if I name this card when playing Feast for Crows?
faq.a: You would complete the search effect and banish The Inquisition before it triggers. Turns out sometimes you do expect them.

faq.q: Can this be moved by force while carrying a minion?
faq.a: Yes.  It cannot take its own steps while carrying a minion.  It can still be moved by force.

faq.q: Can the White Hart's location be attacked?
faq.a: No, the White Hart's ability means that minions and locations which are nearby to the Hart, but are not the Hart, cannot be attacked. Everyone must focus on taking down the White Hart!

faq.q: What happens if a second Pied Piper of Hameln enters play?
faq.a: You apply each of their abilities in timestamp order. The first Piper takes control of all minions with 1 or less power, then the second Piper will take control of them. The controller of the second Piper will end up controlling all minions with 1 or less power.

faq.q: Is this effect limited to once per turn?
faq.a: Nope! You may use it as many times as you want in a turn, if you meet the threshold requirement. Of course, in Constructed play, you'll be limited to four, since you can have at most four Horrible Hybrids in your collection.

faq.q: Do all minions enter the realm tapped, or only minions which would have been Evil?
faq.a: All minion enter the realm tapped.

faq.q: Do multiple castings of this stack? Does it stack with other abilities that cause the minion's damage to heal me?
faq.a: Yes, each instance of an effect like this will trigger and heal you independently.

faq.q: Can this teleport a minion or artifact from a site to the void?
faq.a: No. The location the minion or artifact teleports to must be one diagonal step away from where it started, and steps are only measured within the same region. A minion or artifact starting at a surface location can only be teleported to another surface location, for example.

faq.q: If the Dragonlord gains Ignis Rex's ability, is that considered fire damage? Same question for Adtonitum and air damage?
faq.a: Yes! If the Dragonlord gains Ignis Rex's ability and then discards a fire card, the Dragonlord will deal fire damage. Same answer for Adtonitum and air damage.

faq.q: While my Avatar occupies the surface + void location of The Void site, can I target something occupying the underground + void location of The Void site?
faq.a: Yes! The target is in the same region (void) as the spellcaster, so it can be targeted!

faq.q: If I pay to gain water affinity, does this count as a water site this turn?
faq.a: No, activating this ability means the affinity is granted directly to you for the turn, not applied to the site.

faq.q: What if I choose a Warded minion to destroy?
faq.a: The Ward breaks instead of the minion being destroyed, but there's still an explosion. After the ward breaks (protecting the minion from the destruction effect), it will still take 3 damage along with the other units at its location.

faq.q: What does "an ally flies" mean?
faq.a: The chosen unit takes flying steps as if it had the airborne ability. If the unit cannot take steps (due to being immobile, for instance), it cannot move to the targeted minion.

faq.q: What is a "lone enemy"?
faq.a:
A "lone enemy" is an enemy unit that's not entering simultaneously with another enemy unit. Stationary units at the Troll Bridge ignored.
Here are some examples:
If an enemy [[War Horse]] is carrying its Avatar and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger, since there are two enemies entering simultaneously. 
If your [[Bodach Bogeyman]] is carrying two enemy minions and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger. However, if the Bogeyman were carrying just one enemy, the Bridge would trigger.
If there is already an enemy occupying the Troll Bridge and another enemy unit enters, it will trigger for the entering enemy.

faq.q: What happens if the Trap is animated?
faq.a: The direction it is facing is tracked normally, and is not affected by the Trap's movement or actions.

faq.q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
faq.a: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

faq.q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
faq.a: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

faq.a: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

faq.q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
faq.a: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

faq.q: How do I properly resolve the banish and damage effects?
faq.a: Banish Evil minions first, resolving effects (if any) as a result of their banishment. Then, damage all units occupying those six squares.

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a: Each minion simultaneously deals 1 damage to its site. Then, starting with the active player and then the non-active player, each minion chooses an artifact at it's location to destroy; you must choose an artifact that hasn't been chosen if possible. Then, all the artifacts are simultaneously destroyed. Finally, all minions tap (and won't untap the next time they normally would).

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a: Deal face up, one at a time, taking minions from any cemetery. You choose which minions you deal to each site. The dead minions do not actually "enter" the realm with this effect. Then, damage is dealt simultaneously.

faq.q: Does Harbinger's ability combo with other effects that allow you to cast minions, e.g. Elder Ruins, Troubled Town, Peculiar Port, etc.?
faq.a: Yes! It's effectively a passive ability that can be used whenever you cast a spell on your turn. The golden rule, baby!

faq.q: What is all of the small text on this card?!
faq.a: Don't tell me you entered into a contract with a Demon without reading the fine print! The smaller text is all of the rules and stipulations for the casting of this spell!

faq.q: If I increase or decrease the cost of a magic while I cast it as a Spirit minion, how much power will it have in the realm?
faq.a: Use the printed cost of the magic as its power, regardless of how much mana you actually spent to cast it. Note that magics with X as their cost work appropriately, based on the unmodified cost of the spell when you cast it.

faq.q: Do I still need to meet threshold requirements and pay additional costs, e.g. discarding a site for Craterize?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: Does this count as healing?
faq.a: No, this removes Death's Door and then sets your life to 1.

faq.q: If I cast a magic with X as its cost (e.g. Arcane Barrage) as a Spirit minion, will the minion retain the correct power?
faq.a: Yes, because of the golden rule. If you pay 7 mana for your Arcane Barrage Spirit minion, it will have 7 power while in the realm.

faq.q: Where does the copied spell come from?
faq.a: It's a copy, which is a token, so you have unlimited copies, as needed. It doesn't come from your hand or your deck or anywhere else. It's a token!

faq.q: Does the type of my minions change everywhere, or just in the realm?
faq.a: Everywhere!

faq.q: How does Blood Mana interact with reduced costs?
faq.a: The same cost you would pay with mana is paid by your life instead.

faq.q: Does this ability completely replace their normal type, or simply add a new type?
faq.a: It adds an additional type. For example, your Mortals are Undead and Mortals and would still be silenced by Bower of Bliss. As another example, your Beasts are Monsters and Beasts, so you would still get the discount from a Pond.

faq.q: Can I choose different squares for the damage?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: What if my current life is higher than my maximum life after this effect resolves?
faq.a: Your current life is immediately reduced to your maximum life.

faq.q: If I target an adjacent enemy already sharing a location with Abaddon Succubus, does it still take 2 damage and heal me 2?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: If my summoned minion has a genesis effect, does the genesis resolve before the strike?
faq.a: Yes, resolve the genesis first, including any deathrites. Then, the "strike each other unit" effect resolves.

faq.q: Does this apply if my opponent is searching my deck as well?
faq.a: Yes! Any time your opponent is searching their deck or your deck, they only search the top three cards.

faq.q: Does this buff my opponent's Mortals as well?
faq.a: Yes! The Mayor wants as many votes as possible!

faq.q: What if I cast this while my life is higher than 1?
faq.a: You set your life to 1.

faq.q: What rarity are Avatars for purposes of including them in my collection?
faq.a: Consider Avatars unique for purposes of including them in your collection.

faq.q: If I have Kythera Mechanism and keep "randomly" choosing Chaoswish, can I cast infinite spells?
faq.a: Specify the number of times you cast Chaoswish, and then proceed with the game. Your opponent will have the chance to copy Chaoswish that number of times!

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a: Deal face up to your back row one at a time, placing each card to the surface of a site as you go. Then, shuffle any non-minions and put them on the bottom of your deck. Now all the minions are summoned simultaneously to the location they were dealt to; resolve any effects of those minions being summoned, e.g. genesis effects. Finally, check to see if you're at Death's Door now, and if so, all the summoned minions gain Charge.

faq.q: If Castle Haunt is summoned to a void, e.g. Lucid Dreamers, how does its ability apply?
faq.a: It was never summoned to a site, so it's free to roam around the realm! (Unless it was summoned to The Void site, in which case its restriction applies normally!)

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a: When you would use your avatar's ability (or another ability to play sites without restriction), you may choose to play that site from your collection and banish Ersatz Platz.

faq.q: Can I brand an enemy and step toward the closest Evil on the same turn?
faq.a: No, you must choose only one option each turn.

faq.q: If Selfsame Simulacrum is summoned as a basic copy of an animated magic, what happens?
faq.a: "Basic copy" refers to the printed characteristics of the card, which means Selfsame will try to become a magic. But magics cannot exist in the realm, so Selfsame Simulacrum would immediately go to the cemetery and there would be no effect of the magic. Sorry!

faq.q: If I choose to do 2 damage at one location, do I need to do damage at all the locations in that cardinal direction?
faq.a: Yes. If you choose to resolve this effect, you must deal 2 damage to one unit at each other location in the chosen direction.

faq.q: When moving sites around, does Vindictive Nation protect the nearby sites before or after the move?
faq.a:
Vindictive Nation protects the sites it was nearby before the move. For example:

I = Vindictive Nation
R = Rubble
A = Allied Site
My opponent casts Earthquake and rearranges the two rightmost sites:

Even though site A moved and is now nearby Vindictive Nation, my opponent doesn't lose any life because A wasn't nearby Vindictive Nation before the move.
Alternately, if we started from the second situation and Earthquake moved sites into the first situation, my opponent would lose 3 life because they moved a site that was nearby Vindictive Nation (even though the site ended up no longer nearby).

faq.q: How do I properly resolve this effect?
faq.a:
Choose a cardinal direction from your water site. Forcefully move all enemies from your water site one step in the chosen direction and flood that site. Trigger and resolve any effects related to minions entering or the site being flooded. Then repeat the process until you reach the edge of the realm.
The flood and push effect will continue even across a void, but minions cannot be forcefully moved across regions.
Each site will be flooded at the same moment as the minions arrive, so a submerged minion being evicted will also be submerged on the new site (and there will never be a moment where it's pushed onto the new site without the new site also being flooded).

faq.q: How do I generate a random spell?
faq.a: Click the button on this page!

faq.q: When I determine my three random squares, what if I roll doubles or triples?
faq.a: Reroll any duplicated results until you have three ))unique(( squares.

faq.q: Once I cast a random spell, how do I track it during the game?
faq.a:
Be prepared with index cards + pencil, or some other way to track what gets copied!
Note that a copy is a token, so once it leaves the realm, it's banished per normal token rules. Magics (and any other copy) won't end up in the cemetery.

faq.q: What does "defend alone" mean?
faq.a: When the Defend window closes (see "((Attack))" in the codex for details), If only a single enemy unit uses the Defend ability, the Defender is removed from the fight and the original attack target is reinstated. Defenders still arrive one at a time, but if there's only one, the defense effectively is negated (though that one defender still got to tap and move to the attack's location).

faq.q: If Castle Haunt leaves its summoning site and doesn't immediately die, what happens?
faq.a:
It's free to roam around the realm! This could happen because the Castle Haunt is silenced or disabled as soon as it leaves its summoning site, or because it survives via a Ward upon leaving.
If it ever returns to its summoning site, its ability will apply again if it tries to leave again.

faq.q: Can I brand an enemy in a different region, or one with Stealth?
faq.a: Yes! Branding does not target, and therefore you can choose minions in different regions and/or those with Stealth. This can combo successfully with other cards that care about minions being Evil!

faq.q: Does "has no power here" mean Evil units here have zero power?
faq.a: Yes. Note that when you strike, you determine your power first, then you determine how much damage you deal. So an Evil minion with a Lance would still strike a unit for 1 damage, because it has 0 power and then gets +1 damage from the Lance. See "((Damage))" for more details.

faq.q: Does the site itself get pushed?
faq.a: No.

faq.q: How does summoning burrowed interact with Evil Presence?
faq.a: You may summon the Haunts to an affected site, and they must be burrowed. But the Haunts won't gain Charge and Evil Presence will remain in the realm because the Haunts were not summoned "here" according to Evil Presence, since Evil Presence occupies the surface (and perhaps the void), not underground.

faq.q: Can I pay more life than I have? What if I'm on death's door?
faq.a: You cannot pay more life than you have. If you're on death's door, you won't be able to pay any life and Blood Mana won't help you.

faq.q: Does this count as healing?
faq.a: No, this is setting life.

faq.q: What does it mean to "build The Tower of Babel" and "play ... atop this" ?
faq.a:
You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel.
The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again.
For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel.
