faq.q: If Pith Imp somehow gains Spellcaster, can it pretty please cast the spell it stole?
faq.a: Yes, that does seem fun!

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a: Deal face up, one at a time. Then, draw the voidwalk minions and Monsters, and banish the rest. No minions actually "enter" the realm with this effect.

faq.q: If I have Wormelow Tump in play, what happens?
faq.a: The cemeteries are still swapped, and you protect everything in "your" cemetery (which is really your opponent's).

faq.q: Does my avatar still take the damage, but I just don't lose the game?
faq.a: Correct! Damage is still dealt to your avatar for effects that care about dealing damage. You just don't lose the game as a result!

faq.q: How do I resolve this ability?
faq.a: Fully complete the first attack, including deathrites. Then, Bladedancer must take a step to a different location to be able to attack a new unit (or the same unit if it's oversized and occupies multiple locations). The step cannot be intercepted, but the attack is an actual second attack, following the normal attack sequence.

faq.q: What does "attack out of this site" mean?
faq.a: Take exactly one step away from the site, then attack. It doesn't matter if the unit took steps before entering the Dread Thicket, merely that they take exactly one step away from the Thicket and then attack.

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a:
The first eight times the cat would die, it doesn't instead and fully heals. Track its number of lives in some reasonable way. If it gains a deathrite, it does not trigger on the first eight lives, since it doesn't actually die.
If the cat is moved to an inhospitable location, e.g. underground or underwater, the game will notice and try to kill it along with any other minions who should die. The other minion's deathrite effects will resolve first, and they'll go to the cemetery. Then the game will notice the cat should die, and continue trying to kill it until it's actually dead and goes to the cemetery.

faq.q: Can you "fly to" a minion already sharing your location?
faq.a: No, that's not "flying to." Summon the Guardian Angel to a different location!

faq.q: Are the strikes against other units all simultaneous?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: What happens if the random spell cannot be cast, e.g. no valid target?
faq.a: The spell is not cast, and the next player may copy Chaoswish.

faq.q: If the targeted minion takes less than 2 damage (or no damage at all), do I still heal 2?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: If I cast a magic as a Spirit minion, do I still get the effect of the magic?
faq.a: No. Treat the textbox of the magic as entirely blank, though it retains its elements and rarity. For example, if you cast Craterize as Spirit minion, you do not need to discard a site as an additional cost, and it will be summoned as an 8 power, Elite earth minion.

faq.q: Can I brand an enemy who can't be modified, e.g. Monks of Kobalsa?
faq.a: Yes, you can still brand them, and your cards will still treat them as Evil. They aren't actually being modified or becoming Evil; your cards just treat them that way.

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect?
faq.a:
If you cast Mephistopheles, your Avatar is banished. Mephistopheles is now your Avatar. He retains Unique rarity, Demon type, and Air element, but he's no longer a minion and only an Avatar. Your current and maximum life remain the same. Notably, you won't be able to play sites normally because Mephistopheles doesn't have that ability. You will still be able to cast spells because Avatars are spellcasters as one of their characteristics.
If you manage to summon Mephistopheles without casting him, then he will not replace your avatar, but his second ability will still function.

faq.q: What does "cards or allies" mean?
faq.a: Cards in their hand, or allies in the realm.

faq.q: When does the enemy avatar have the opportunity to pay life?
faq.a: Immediately after the strike, before deathrites resolve. For example, if your strike puts them to 2 or less life, they will not be able to pay 3 life.

faq.q: On my turn when I go to Death's Door, can I still take damage and lose life?
faq.a: Yes. You cannot lose the game due to taking damage, but taking damage and losing life will reduce your life total if possible. See "((Death's Door))" for more details.

faq.q: When counting "each unit," do I include all adjacent squares?
faq.a: Yes! Count any unit in any square adjacent to the summoning square (including the summoning square itself). Each unit counts once, regardless of how many adjacent squares it occupies.

faq.q: What if Kairos dies on The Geistwood?
faq.a: Since the deathrite effect and genesis effect will be triggered simultaneously, you may order them as you wish. If you resolve the printed deathrite first, archived cards will return to their recorded state, then the printed genesis effect will not resolve, since Kairos is banished. If you resolve the printed genesis first (as a deathrite due to The Geistwood), the realm will be archived, and then when the printed deathrite resolves, it would return to that very recently archived state, and Kairos would be banished.

faq.q: If my Vindictive Nation is silenced by my opponent, e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak, will my opponent lose life?
faq.a: Yes! Silence from Smokestacks is applied as a passive ability, but the act of silencing literally triggers Vindictive Nation's ability. So as Vindictive Nation becomes silenced, its ability triggers. See the ((Triggered Ability)) codex entry for details.

faq.q: When I flee, is it step by step movement or teleportation?
faq.a: It's step by step movement!

faq.q: Is this an activated ability that I use while Slimy Mutants are in my hand?
faq.a: Yes! While Slimy Mutants are in your hand, you may pay (3) and resolve the effect.

faq.q: If there are two Rivers of Blood in play, do they stack?
faq.a: Yes. Half the healing (rounding down), then half the healing again (round down). So [[Divine Healing]] would heal 1 with two Rivers of Blood in play.

faq.q: If Michael cannot take a step, does he still get to strike?
faq.a: Yes, but you must declare a legal step if you can, using the normal lookahead rules described in "Range of Motion."

faq.q: Do I pick left or right for all units together, or can I choose different directions?
faq.a: Choose left or right, and apply it to every unit at land sites in the column.

faq.q: If there are multiple Apostles of Thamariel in play, do I need to track which Apostles go with which Angels?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: How does this resolve if I summon an oversized minion?
faq.a: At least one of the summoning sites must include an affected site. The "strike each other unit where it lands" effect occurs on one affected site of your choice (that the summoned minion occupies).

faq.q: What if the random spell has additional costs, e.g. Craterize?
faq.a: When you cast "((for free))," you don't pay any additional costs. Have fun!

faq.q: If my magic targets my allied minion, does that qualify as "chooses" for the Book of Blessing?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: What if an effect directs me to draw a spell, but it turns out there's a site on top of my spellbook?
faq.a: All cards in your spellbook are considered spells while in your spellbook, so you can draw it normally.

faq.q: What happens if I impersonate the Druid and then use the ability to flip?
faq.a: You will summon Bruin, flip, ... and then immediately lose the game because you no longer have an Avatar in play! Maybe don't include Druid in your collection?

faq.q: What if an effect directs me to draw a site?
faq.a:
You have no atlas, and thus any effect that causes you to draw sites will not resolve. You don't draw any cards and you don't lose the game.
You cannot choose to draw from your atlas in your start phase.

faq.q: Can this minion die?
faq.a: The only way it can be killed is if you sacrifice it. Otherwise, it cannot be killed. Meet your doom!

faq.q: What if there was more than one killer last turn?
faq.a: Bitter Departed may teleport to any one of the killers to strike it.

faq.q: Does this effect have time to resolve if the site itself is getting destroyed?
faq.a: Yes! They are very vindictive.

faq.q: If my opponent has a warded minion and I brand it as Evil, does it lose Ward?
faq.a: No, because only your cards treat it as Evil. Also, branding does not target, so Ward won't break for that reason either.

faq.q: What if an effect specifies a spell or site from a zone other than my spellbook?
faq.a:
If an effect cares about spell vs. site while the card is outside of your spellbook, you must follow the effect correctly at the moment the effect resolves.
Several examples:
If resolve Stone Rain, you must honestly state how many sites you have in your hand at that moment.
You can partially remove cards from their sleeves and show the back to demonstrate the accurate count to your opponent, or call a judge in a tournament if you have foil cards (or double sleeve your cards with different inner color sleeves in the case of foils).
If your opponent plays Pith Imp, you must honestly specify your spells in hand, and randomly select from only those.
If your opponent attacks your Wizard's Den for the first time and you don't have any spells in hand, you must honestly demonstrate to your opponent that you only have sites in hand.
If you play Sisters of Avalon and have no spells in hand, you must honestly demonstrate to your opponent that you have no spells.
After an effect resolves that requires you to reveal the number of spells and sites in your hand, you may then mix up the cards in your hand again so that your opponent doesn't know which cards are spells and which are sites.

faq.q: Normally pull effects can't cross regional boundaries. Can I actually pull the target minion into the void?
faq.a: Yes, obviously!

faq.q: Must I choose which of my spellcasters is casting the spell before I know what it is?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: If I do 1 damage to three minions simultaneously, does the Barricade break?
faq.a: Yes, because 1+1+1 = 3 damage dealt all at the same time.

faq.q: When exactly is "after striking" ?
faq.a: After effects concurrent with striking (e.g. after gaining life via Daperyll Vampire), but before any Deathrite abilities resolve. It's in the same moment that Stealth would break due to striking.

faq.q: Does this effect count all wards in the realm, or only ones I control?
faq.a: It counts all wards in the realm, on any unit or site!

faq.q: If damage is prevented, do I still heal?
faq.a: No. Flagellant must actually take 1 or more damage for you to heal.

faq.q: If the Army moves through many locations (e.g. Grapple Shot, Seven-league Boots), does it leave many Skeletons behind?
faq.a: Yes! Leave a Skeleton behind each time the Army enters a new location (or takes damage).

faq.q: Does "modifying" a site include Flooding it?
faq.a: Yes, since Flooded is an ability that gets added to the site.

faq.q: After fleeing, if I somehow fail to reach the Sanctuary, do I still gain the Ward?
faq.a: No!

faq.q: Can I choose different directions for each card being pushed?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Is the site played adjacent to the Clay Golem, superseding normal site placement rules?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: Does this need to be carried to have an effect?
faq.a: Yes, since "you" or "your" refers to the controller of the artifact, and carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled.

faq.q: Does this need to be carried to have an effect?
faq.a: Yes, since "you" or "your" refers to the controller of the artifact, and carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled.

faq.q: If I break two allied Wards to increase the damage, will it be three instances of 1 damage each, or 3 damage once?
faq.a: Three damage once.

faq.q: If there are an even number of Mismanaged Mortuaries in play, do they cancel out?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does this effect target the minion?
faq.a: No! Therefore, the banished minion can be in a different region and/or have Stealth.

faq.q: What is "lower" rarity?
faq.a: The order of rarities (from highest to lowest) is: Unique, Elite, Exceptional, and Ordinary. For example, if you control an Exceptional Demon, you could search for an Exceptional or Ordinary spell.

faq.q: Is the damage dealt simultaneously?
faq.a: Yes. For example, if you have a 5 power Monster, it will deal 1+1+1+1+1, all simultaneously. If you try dealing it to a warded unit, the Ward will prevent all of it. If your opponent has Shield Maidens nearby, each damage will be reduced. If you have Panpipes of Pnom, it will be 2+2+2+2+2 damage instead.

faq.q: If Deathspeaker uses his ability to cast Skeleton Mage, does the Skeleton Mage get to use its genesis ability (casting and resolving a spell) before being banished?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: What happens if the next spell I cast is Twist of Fate?
faq.a: Let's say your life is 16 and my life is 20. Therefore, you cast Twist of Fate for 4 mana, but instead of mana, you pay 4 life. Your life is now 12 and the magic goes onto the Storyline. The magic resolves, swapping our life totals. My life is now 12 and your life is 20. Tricky!

faq.q: What happens if I play Courtesan Thaïs and then immediately play Chaoswish on the same turn?
faq.a:
It's still your turn, so your opponent still controls their own choices. They can freely choose to copy Chaoswish or not.
On the other hand, if you cast Courtesan Thaïs first, then on your opponent's turn (which you're controlling) you see that they have Chaoswish in hand and you cast it for them, you can keep copying Chaoswish as long as you want; you will decide for yourself and you will decide for them (since you're controlling their turn).

faq.q: If Flagellant takes 5 damage, do I heal more than 1?
faq.a: No, just 1. But if Flagellant took 1 damage separately five times, e.g. Abyssal Assault or Arcane Barrage, you would heal 5.

faq.q: Am I required to sleeve my cards, and if so, how should I do it?
faq.a: You are required to sleeve your cards, and they should all be the same. Cards in your spellbook and collection should be indistinguishable whether they are sites or spells.

faq.q: If an avatar has an odd maximum life, do they round down after halving it?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
faq.a: Yes!

faq.q: Does this effect span the void?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: How does this ability impact my collection?
faq.a: You may include any cards you wish in your collection, following normal deckbuilding rules. If you have 0 copies of a unique card in your deck, you may include 1 ))copy(( in your collection. If you have 2 copies of a unique card in your deck, you cannot include any copies in your collection.

faq.q: If my opponent and I keep deciding to copy Chaoswish, what happens?
faq.a:
You have a lot of fun?
In a tournament setting, you'll probably hit the round time limit eventually.

faq.q: What happens if I strike for 0 damage?
faq.a: A strike for zero damage is still considered a strike, so it will still trigger Interrogator's ability.

faq.q: When determining "closest Evil," do I only consider units in my region?
faq.a: Yes! See "((Closest))" for more details.

faq.q: If a warded Angel Ascendant fights another minion, the ward will break when the strike happens. So does Angel Ascendant strike for 2 or 3?
faq.a: It will strike for 3 (with the +1 power from Ward). If the opposing minion somehow struck first (perhaps via a Lance), then the ward would indeed break first and then the Angel Ascendant would only strike back for 2.

faq.q: Can your avatar end up in the void after Kairos dies, and if so, what happens?
faq.a: It's theoretically possible! If it does happen, the mandatory actions rule will apply to you, and if you have a site in hand, you'll be required to play it. The way it could happen is left as an exercise for the reader!

faq.q: Is the state of the Storyline archived? Does the Storyline get restored to its snapshotted state?
faq.a:
No! The Storyline isn't archived, and it simply continues to resolve normally after Kairos's deathrite.
For example, I have Infernal Legion in the realm on square 8. Then I summon Kairos and the realm is archived. The Infernal Legion moves to square 3, and I summon Vatn Draconis. During my End Phase, I have ((simultaneous triggers)) for Infernal Legion and Vatn Draconis. I choose to order the storyline with Vatn Draconis first, then Infernal Legion. So I resolve Vatn Draconis's ability, which kills Kairos. Kairos's deathrite goes on the storyline and resolves before the Infernal Legion ability. When I archived the realm, the storyline was empty. But that doesn't matter because the storyline is different from the realm. We return cards to their recorded state, placing the Infernal Legion back on square 8, and then continue resolving the current storyline, so the Infernal Legion's ability resolves when it's on square 8, even though the ability was added to the storyline when the Legion was on square 3.

faq.q: Is the damage resolved one at a time, after each hit?
faq.a: Yes! Resolve the damage (and any deathrites) from the first hit, then bounce for the second hit, resolving that damage, then bounce and resolve the third hit.

faq.q: Can I hit the caster or other allies with this?
faq.a: At the first location of the projectile’s path, it cannot hit allies or the caster, even if it hits an enemy there first. If the Ball Lightning leaves the first location, it could bounce back and hit allies or the caster later in its path.

faq.q: How does Merlin’s ability work and what does “any time” actually permit?
faq.a: This is a passive ability, usable any time on your turn, including during your start phase before you draw a card. But, you may still only cast spells when they are normally permitted to be cast (i.e. during your Main Phase when nothing else is on the storyline other than this ability). Technically, if a Crave Golem were attacking during your Start Phase, Merlin could cast a Dodge Roll then!

faq.q: Can you “pull apart” a row with a single site?
faq.a: No. That’s not what “pull apart” means.

faq.q: What does “wherever she is" mean?
faq.a: Anywhere! The realm, your hand, and cemetery, and even while in the middle of your spellbook.

faq.q: Since Avatars are Spellcasters, is Vivien a Spellcaster?
faq.a: Not by default. Avatars don’t have the printed ability “Spellcaster,” so Vivien must gain the Spellcaster ability another way, e.g. a minion with the printed Spellcaster ability.

faq.q: Can Vivien the Enchantress copy the abilities of another Vivien the Enchantress?
faq.a: No.

faq.q: What happens if Vivien uses the Druid’s ability to summon Bruin and flip?
faq.a: She summons Bruin and then flips. As a flipped card with nothing on the back, she has no game text and will effectively do nothing for the rest of the game. She is no longer a minion, has no card type or abilities, etc. The flipped card can exist in the void, and technically she could turn off Pristine Paradise, and would be destroyed by Roots of Yggdrasil.

faq.q: When I cast one of the banished spells, is that placed back in the cemetery?
faq.a: No. There's no way back from being banished, which overrides the part of resolution that would place the card in the cemetery.

faq.q: When I use the Archimago’s ability to banish 3 magic spells and cast 1, do I still have to pay mana and meet threshold?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: When using this ability, must the Archimago be the caster?
faq.a: No, any of your spellcasters can cast the copied spell.

faq.q: What happens if I pay the cost of banishing three spells, but I cannot actually cast any of those three?
faq.a: If you cannot cast any of those three spells, they remain banished and nothing else happens. You did not cast a spell. (If you can cast one of the three, you must.)

faq.q: Does the Druid's flip side ability work with Poisonous Dagger?
faq.a: No. The site itself gains the ability and is doing the damage.

faq.q: Can the Druid's flip side ability give the Druid kill credit?
faq.a: No. Only units can get kill credit, and the site is source of the damage. The triggered ability is the site's ability, not the Druid's. See the "((kill credit))" codex entry for more details.

faq.q: If a site loses its abilities, does the Druid's flip side ability still apply? Can this affect Bedrock?
faq.a: No. The Druid grants an ability to the site. If the site is silenced (or can't be modified in the case of Bedrock), then it loses the ability and will not deal damage.

faq.q: How does this work?
faq.a: After the throw, Rhongomyniad is in the final location along its path, and is not carried by any unit.

faq.q: Can my Free City be struck by opposing units, and if so, will it take damage?
faq.a: Yes, it can be struck, and any strike damage to your Free City will cause your avatar to ))lose(( the same amount of life.

faq.q: What happens if there are two Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby each other?
faq.a: See "((Example - Two Smokestacks of Gnaak))" in the codex!

faq.q: What is a technical definition of what’s happening when you use this card’s ability?
faq.a: Choose a row or column with two adjacent sites and at least one void. Then, “pull apart” the two adjacent sites as follows: one site stays in its current square, and the other site (along with all other contiguous sites in its row or column) shifts one square. Put Rift Valley in the void that was just created. The shifting of sites and the arrival of Rift Valley happen simultaneously.

faq.q: If it tries to become a basic copy of an aura animated by Enchantress, what happens?
faq.a: Selfsame Simulacrum becomes an aura (not a minion), since that’s the actual text on the animated aura. As soon as Selfsame Simulacrum is an aura, it expands to its proper size based on card text (and default aura rules), and must continue to occupy the location that was specified during casting.

faq.q: Does this affect subsurface units?
faq.a: No. (They are not atop the site.)

faq.q: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
faq.a: An animated Wall of Air can’t move (unless it gains power), since it has a Wall of Air in its middle! If it gains power (or teleports) and manages to move, the Wall of Air applies between the two squares it occupies.

faq.q: If the Battlemage attacks and kills two enemies in a single fight (if my opponent chose to include multiple defenders), does the Battlemage draw two cards?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
What does “passes through” mean?
faq.a: Moving through in any way, whether willingly or by force. For example, a unit moved by Grapple Shot or Pudge Butcher would take damage from the Wall of Fire. Note that a teleported unit doesn’t pass through borders, and thus wouldn't be affected.

faq.q: Does this affect Airborne units?
faq.a: Yes. (They are atop the site.)

faq.q: Does this affect the corners of the border? (e.g. Airborne units moving diagonally)
faq.a: No. "Border" means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

faq.q: Does this affect the corners of the border? (e.g. Airborne units moving diagonally)
faq.a: No. "Border" means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

faq.q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
Does the path include the starting and ending locations?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: How does this work with end of turn and damage clearing?
faq.a: The intent is that a 1 power minion with 1 damage + the Trinket would survive the turn.

faq.q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
faq.a: The beta text is correct.

faq.q: Do I pay all the costs and choose all the targets when the spell is cast?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: How can I tell if a spell or non-basic ability targets something?
faq.a: It will use the word “target.”

faq.q: What does "your location" mean?
faq.a: In this case, “your location” means "a location that your avatar occupies."

faq.q: What does “can’t move itself away” mean?
faq.a: Cerberus can't choose to move to a location that is farther from your avatar than its current location. (Count distance using steps that Cerberus would take using its own modes of movement, e.g. Airborne if it gained it somehow.)

faq.q: Does the damage resolve sequentially or simultaneously?
faq.a: All targets take the damage simultaneously.

faq.q: If your avatar occupies a site you don't control, can you summon Cerberus there?
faq.a: No. The first sentence is an additional restriction on summoning.

faq.q: When is the power doubled?
faq.a: This effect applies a doubling throughout the turn. If the unit gains or loses power, apply any additions or subtractions first, then double.

faq.q: What does "alone here" mean?
faq.a: No other units at the location.

faq.q: What counts as "playing" a card?
faq.a: Playing a site, which costs 0, or casting a spell.

faq.q: If I have Crusade or House Arn Bannermen affecting my Gnome Hollows, may I summon a 2-power minion there?
faq.a: Yes. It's first summoned (enters the realm), then ongoing effects are applied (e.g. Crusade).

faq.q: Do I really have to rip it to pieces?
faq.a: Please see the golden rule! The point is to actually, literally rip the card up, so it will never be playable again. It is banished after you rip it.

faq.q: Can you play Rift Valley into an area affected by Atlantean Fate?
faq.a: Yes, since Atlantean Fate only affects the site once it’s already in play, and Rift Valley modifies how it’s played in the first place.

faq.q: Can you play Rift Valley into an area affected by Atlantean Fate?
faq.a: Yes, since Atlantean Fate only affects the site once it’s already in play, and Rift Valley modifies how it’s played in the first place.

faq.q: If I have two (e.g. via Replication), do the effects stack?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Can the bearer shoot or defend against a stealthed enemy?
faq.a: Yes. The bearer can target stealthed minions with spells, shoot them with projectiles, attack or intercept them and even defend against their attacks.

faq.q: If attacked by a minion that strikes first, does the Giantess end up striking back?
faq.a: Yes, assuming she isn't killed.

faq.q: If River of Flame casts a spell, choosing the surface, but there are Maddening Bells underground, is the River of Flame affected?
faq.a: Yes! Those bells are so loud (and still nearby the caster).

faq.q: Can it burrow and unburrow different things the same turn?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does Undertow let you pull a unit underwater if they have submerge?
faq.a: No, because it’s a “normal step,” which doesn’t allow changing regions.

faq.q: If I control Rubble, can my opponent still play a site there?

faq.a:
First, identify all the minions that Crave Golem ))can attack(( within its range of motion.
If there are one or more such minions:
Randomly pick one, then move (if needed), and attack it. This counts as a normal attack and may be defended.

If there are no such minions:

If not, it doesn't move and the ability is over.
If so, take one step toward the minion that requires the fewest Crave Golem steps to reach. (Crave Golem's controller's choice if tied.) This movement cannot be intercepted.

You cast the minion spell.
Pay mana, meet threshold, banish it from the cemetery, identify where it will be summoned.
The minion enters the the realm. (It is a copy of the banished minion.)
"Enter the ))realm((" effects trigger and resolve. These include:
Genesis abilities.
Effects like Wayfaring Pilgrim, Giant Shark, Mariner's Curse, Bottomless Pit, etc. See "((Simultaneous Triggers))" in the Codex for more details.
The minion is banished.
The intent is that the Deathspeaker can speak to the dead, invoke their abilities, and then release them into the afterlife (whatever that may be).
See also "((Splitting Events on the Storyline))" and the example with Tawny plus a site's genesis. faq.q: If I Grapple Shot a minion with Submerge through an area affected by Mariner's Curse, what happens?
faq.a: When the Grapple Shot projectile hits the unit, the game adds specific movement steps for the ally to the Storyline: Move A (surface) -> B (surface), Move B (surface) -> C (surface). Then, we start resolving those steps. If Mariner's Curse is on site B, once the unit being dragged reaches site B, it will be submerged, and live. Then the game tries to resolve Move B (surface) -> C (surface), which fails, since the unit isn't on the surface of site B anymore. Thus, there's no strike from Grapple Shot since it didn't reach the hit unit's location.

faq.q: What happens if Megamoeba gains burrow or submerge?
faq.a: It can occupy both the surface location and the subsurface location on a site, and each occupied location will grant +1 power, per card text. 40 power Megamoeba, here we come!

faq.q: What happens if Megamoeba is forcefully burrowed or submerged without the burrow or submerge ability?
faq.a: If any part of unit occupies an inhospitable location, it dies. So, the Megamoeba would die in this case.

faq.q: What happens when the Megamoeba gets carried?
faq.a: It occupied all the locations it was carried through.

faq.q: If a minion has voidwalk and is in the void, could Backstab move it to an adjacent site to strike a tapped minion there?
faq.a: No. Your spellcaster must target both minions (which are in different regions), but that's impossible since you pick a single location the spellcaster occupies for casting a spell. You can only target minions in the region where the spell is being cast. See "((Casting Spells))" for more details.

faq.q: Does “here” mean Mother Nature’s location or site?
faq.a: “Here” references Mother Nature’s exact location.

faq.q: Are there any other corner cases for Magellan Globe?
faq.a: I think you mean edge cases! Let us know if you think of any more we should add. In general, apply the golden rule and have fun!

faq.q: What does “enter this site on the ground” mean?
faq.a: Entering on the ground only covers movement from the surface of another site to the surface of the Mountain Pass, excluding Airborne and teleportation.

faq.q: I have a minion on my Mountain Pass, and a voidwalk minion on an adjacent square. Can I move from the void to Mountain Pass?
faq.a: Yes, since moving on the ground requires the unit to start from the surface of a site. Since the void isn’t a site, moving from the void to Mountain Pass isn’t considered moving on the ground.

faq.q: Does Mirror Realm (copying an earth site), Valley of Delight (choosing earth), or one of the Bloom sites (i.e. Twilight Bloom) count for Geomancer's first ability?
faq.a: Yes. Mirror ))Realm(( works because it applies as it enters the realm. Valley of Delight and the Bloom sites work because the Genesis effect of the site interrupts the resolution of the Geomancer's ability; when the second part of Geomancer's ability actually resolves and looks at the site, the site is indeed an earth (E) site. See "((Splitting Events on the Storyline))" for more details on Valley of Delight interaction, analogous to the Tawny example and splitting the Druid's ability.

faq.q: Normally, when moving from void to a site, a minion (e.g. Hounds of Ondaros) can move directly to the surface OR subsurface. Therefore, when moving from the subsurface + void location of this site, can a minion like Hounds of Ondaros move directly to the surface of an adjacent site? Could they move from the surface + void location directly to the subsurface of an adjacent site?
faq.a: Yes! Minions with voidwalk can continue to use their voidwalk abilities to move accordingly.

faq.a: Jack will enter at the King's location and will technically change control briefly to the controller of the [[King of the Realm]], but his ability will already be on the storyline. Jack will then silence and kill the King, and return to your control.

faq.q: How does the Bureau interact with Wormelow Tump?
faq.a: You still have to pay the Bureau tax! The cards themselves are not being affected; a separate cost is being added to allow you to access them.

faq.q: How does this ability work?
faq.a: It is an activated ability that you can choose to activate one time on your turn. You choose a minion that is on a connected river, and push it one step. You can use this to push the minion off of rivers, and you can activate it even if River Rapids is the only "connected" river.

faq.q: How do I resolve this effect if control of the minion changes between fights (e.g. it had Infiltrate cast on it earlier)?
faq.a:
If control of the ally changes in the middle of resolving this effect, the units it sees as "enemies" will change as well.  The caster of Blaze of Glory still chooses the order in which the fights happen. Note that the fights are not optional.
For example, I've infiltrated your Autumn Unicorn. You also have a Lugbog Cat and a Skeleton nearby, while I have a Bosk Troll nearby. I cast Blaze of Glory on the Autumn Unicorn. I choose to have it fight your Skeleton first, which breaks stealth, returning control of the Unicorn to you. The Skeleton is removed from the realm. The Unicorn isn't done fighting yet because it still sees an enemy - the Bosk Troll! So the Unicorn fights the Bosk Troll. The Bosk Troll dies and is placed in the cemetery. Then the Unicorn dies and is placed in the cemetery.
That is, after each fight, look around and ask "Are there any nearby enemies I haven't fought yet?" If there is, fight one! Repeat until there are no unfought nearby enemies.

faq.q: Does this mean that minions which are not in the realm are not Evil as well?
faq.a: No minion anywhere is Evil as long as the Saint is in play.  This means that if a player casts [[Black Mass]], they will not be able to reveal any minions, as none of them can be Evil.

faq.q: Can this teleport an aura from a site to the void?
faq.a: Yes! When moving auras, you ignore the regional boundaries between surface and void locations.

faq.q: What happens if I impersonate the Realm-Eater, use the ability to destroy a site, and then take damage or otherwise lose that mask before I can digest?
faq.a: The Realm-Eater's ability will have created an ongoing effect which immobilizes you, and can only be removed by activating the "digest" ability.  If you lose that ability, you cannot remove the immobile effect.  Be careful!

faq.q: What if an oversized unit is involved?
faq.a: Choose one of the locations the oversized unit occupies as the destination of the other card. See "((Teleporting Oversized Units))" for more details.

faq.q: If an effect grants this free movement (e.g. Arcade of Bones), can I spawn infinite Skeleton tokens?
faq.a:
No. Whenever you declare a movement path, you cannot repeat specific steps. Lets say we have sites arranged like this in a row, with Army of the Dead starting on site A, along with an [[Arcade of Bones]]:

You could declare the following movement path for the Army:
A to B
B to C
C to B
B to A
None of those steps repeat exactly, so it's all perfectly legal, and you would spawn a Skeleton for each of those steps, for a total of 4 Skeletons spawned. You cannot, however, put another A to B step on the path, since that would be a repeat of the first step.

faq.q: Using Dream-Quest, can I put to sleep one of my non-minion Spellcasters (e.g. Omphalos, River of Flame) or a spellcaster with restrictions (e.g. Earl of the Ivory Towers, Wind Sylph)?
faq.a:
Yes!
An Omphalos will be disabled and thus not draw a spell that turn, but it cannot be hurt unless it's animated. Assuming it is not hurt, you may wake it up at the start of your next turn.
For a site (e.g. River of Flame), it provides no Threshold while disabled, but it will wake up in time to produce mana next turn, due to the order of resolution in the Start Phase.

faq.a: You technically can, but beware! If the first Craterize successfully destroys the targeted site, the second Craterize will no longer have a valid target in the realm and will fail, resulting in no damage from that copy of Craterize.

faq.q: Can I choose to move a step forward and then back to strike an enemy twice with this?
faq.a: No. You can choose to step forward and back, but an enemy is either along your path or not. They will not be struck more than once.

faq.q: What happens if Mirror Realm copies a Rubble?
faq.a: If Mirror Realm copies a Rubble, you gain no mana. You still control the Rubble, it can be attacked normally, you can play sites adjacent to it, it can be replaced by a site normally, etc. Track it carefully, distinct from other uncontrolled Rubble in the realm.

faq.q: When using the Deathspeaker's ability, are passive abilities applied before the banishing effect? The updated text only mentions Genesis abilities.
faq.a: Yes, the minion is in the realm for a brief moment, so any passive abilities it has will be applied during that window before it is banished.

faq.q: If Pathfinder cannot move to the played site because of some effect (e.g. Sphere of Animosity, Quagmire) can you still play the site?
faq.a: Yes, you can still play the site to a void or rubble adjacent to the Pathfinder, even if you know you cannot move to it (Sphere of Animosity) or an effect from the played site immediately stops the Pathfinder from being able to move (Quagmire).

faq.q: What counts as an "enemy" for this effect? Is it enemies of the beast, or enemies of the site?
faq.a: Beasts at Varmint Warrens cannot be targeted by spells or abilities used by the enemies of the beast. All kinds of critters can hide in the warrens!

faq.q: Does it continue to provide fire affinity after it transforms into a Demon?
faq.a: Yes. The transformed Demon provides affinity, due to the golden rule. Obviously, if the Demon dies, you will lose that affinity.

faq.q: When an avatar is stretched by this effect, does it count as entering the new location?
faq.a: Yes! The avatar has to be able to enter the location for the effect to work, and then it will trigger any effects caused by entering. It does not count as moving, however.

faq.q: What happens if the ally strikes the avatar during a fight, and is killed by the avatar's strike?
faq.a: If the ally dies as a result of the fight, then you are unable to drag both the ally and the avatar to the Dungeon.  The avatar will not move.

faq.q: What happens if I cast Lacuna Entity to a void location and then pull in a minion with a passive ability which will silence or disable the Entity?
faq.a:
If the Entity pulls in something which will remove its abilities (e.g. [[Sisters of Silence]]) then the Entity will briefly find itself in the void without the voidwalk ability, and will be banished. It will have already pulled the other minion to its location, however.
Note that if it pulls in a minion which disables other minions "at rest," such as a [[Hillock Basilisk]], the Entity will not be at rest until after that minion has finished moving and passives are applied. This means the Basilisk would be banished before it could disable the Entity.

faq.q: Can the Bullfrog choose to drop the minion it swallowed?
faq.a: No, it can't choose to drop the swallowed minion. (If the swallowed minion is teleported away, it will still be automatically dropped.)

faq.a: No, Pathfinder's ability specifies that the site must come from the top of your Atlas.

faq.a: Since transform effects permanently change the characteristics of the card, as opposed to temporary modifications of characteristics (i.e. [[Overpower]]), the copy effect will take on those new characteristics.  For instance, a [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] copying an [[Island Leviathan]] that has been transformed will enter play as an 8-power Monster minion that provides one water affinity.

faq.q: What happens if an oversized avatar is occupying a site, and then some effect moves that site?
faq.a:
When a site moves, only things of "normal" size move with it. As the avatar is now oversized, it will not be moved.
In most cases when a site moves, another site will be left in its place (e.g. [[Rift Valley]]). In these situations, the avatar will end up occupying the surface of the new site. In the case of [[Cloud City]], which leaves a void location behind, the avatar will now be occupying that void square. See ((mandatory actions)) for what happens if your avatar is in the void.
Note that in both cases the avatar does not "enter" the new location that it is occupying.
